extraction.name: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, consisting of multiple-choice question-answer pairs derived from how-to instructions. The dataset tests the ability of natural language understanding models to link text to a robust intuitive-physics model of the world.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by asking annotators to provide semantic perturbations or alternative approaches inspired by instructions from instructables.com. Annotators were prompted to construct goal-solution pairs and 'tricks' (incorrect but plausible solutions). The data was then cleaned using the AFLite algorithm to remove annotation artifacts and biases.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The AFLite algorithm was used to perform systematic data bias reduction by discarding instances whose feature representations were collectively highly indicative of the target label. Examples with low agreement during validation were removed.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm. Examples were truncated at 150 tokens. The dataset was split into training, development, and test sets, with the train, development, and test folds automatically produced by AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to glance at instructions from instructables.com and construct two component tasks: a physical goal, a valid solution, and a 'trick' (an invalid but subtly plausible solution). Annotators were seeded with instructables from six categories. A qualification HIT was used to ensure annotator quality. An interface included a diff button to highlight differences between solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (implied by 'HIT', 'onturkerview.com', and 'Annotator pay')
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed, particularly those requiring expert-level knowledge. Annotators were free to create clever tricks, often differing by as little as one word. The diff button improved annotator accuracy and speed.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: AFLite algorithm, BERT-Large, Spacy, GPT BPE tokenizer
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to bridge the representational gap in AI by evaluating language representations on physical commonsense, which is critical for tasks like robotics and human-AI interaction. It highlights limitations in current models regarding physical world understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset addresses reporting bias by using instructables to encourage atypical solutions. However, it acknowledges that models may still rely on spurious biases, which AFLite attempts to mitigate. The dataset focuses on everyday objects and situations, potentially limiting generalization to other domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to English. It focuses on everyday physical commonsense, which may not cover all types of physical reasoning. Some 'mistakes' by models were found to be correct but required web search to verify. The dataset is adversarial to certain models like BERT.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding, evaluating large-scale pretrained language models, and diagnosing physical understanding in deep learning models.
